UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within the TOOLROOM2.0 application. This entity stores non-authentication related user data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

username.description: A unique username chosen by the user.

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Defines categories for organizing tools, enabling efficient browsing and filtering.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: The name of the category (e.g., 'Hand Tools', 'Power Tools', 'Measurement').

description.description: A brief description of the category.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the category was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the category was last updated.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a descriptive tag used to further organize and discover tools through a flexible keyword system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tag entity.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the tag was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the tag was last updated.

Tool.title: Tool
Tool.description: Represents a single tool or resource managed within the TOOLROOM2.0 catalog, including its details, status, and associations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tool entity.

name.description: The official name or title of the tool.

description.description: A detailed description of the tool, its purpose, and features.

imageUrl.description: URL to an image of the tool for visual identification.

quantity.description: The current number of this specific tool available in the inventory.

location.description: The physical storage location of the tool (e.g., 'Shelf 3A', 'Toolbox Drawer 2').

status.description: The current operational status of the tool (e.g., 'available', 'in-use', 'maintenance', 'lost').

ownerId.description: Reference to UserProfile. Indicates which user 'owns' or is primarily responsible for this tool. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Tool)

categoryId.description: Reference to Category. Specifies the main category this tool belongs to. (Relationship: Category 1:N Tool)

tagIds.description: References to Tags. A list of unique identifiers for tags associated with this tool. (Relationship: Tag N:N Tool)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the tool record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the tool record was last updated.

definition.description: A global catalog of all tools within the system. Readable by all authenticated users. Writable by the tool's 'ownerId' or by an administrator. Includes denormalized 'ownerId' for authorization independence, enabling robust QAP for read and efficient write access control.

definition.description: A marker collection for Database Access Control (DBAC). The existence of a document at this path, where 'userId' matches 'request.auth.uid', grants global administrative privileges. The 'Tag' schema is used as a generic document type to satisfy schema requirements, as a dedicated 'Role' entity schema is not provided.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user designated as an administrator.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for TOOLROOM2.0 is designed around the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and DBAC, ensuring robust security and debuggability. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **UserProfile:** User profiles are stored in `/user_profiles/{userId}`. Authorization is path-based, with rules directly checking `request.auth.uid == userId`. This removes the need for `get()` calls to verify ownership, making profile access atomic and debuggable.
2.  **Category & Tag:** These collections (`/categories/{categoryId}` and `/tags/{tagId}`) are global reference data, readable by all authenticated users. Write access is restricted to administrators, determined by checking for the *existence* of a document in the `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection (as explained below). This `exists()` check is a direct lookup by `request.auth.uid` and does not rely on content or `get()` operations, maintaining independence.
3.  **Tool:** Tools are stored in a top-level collection `/tools/{toolId}`. The `ownerId` field is denormalized directly within each `Tool` document. This is critical for authorization independence: write rules for tools can directly check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId` or `exists(/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` without needing to perform a `get()` call to a parent document or another collection to determine ownership or management rights. This allows for atomic `create` and `update` operations and simplifies rule logic.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **UserProfile:** While technically allowing `list`, rules would typically limit listing to the authenticated user's own profile (effectively a `get` operation for their specific document), or require admin privileges for broader listing. This ensures that unauthorized wide-ranging queries are prevented.
2.  **Category & Tag:** These collections are explicitly designed for global readability (`allow list: if request.auth.uid != null`). This perfectly supports the 'Advanced Search & Filtering' feature, allowing clients to fetch all categories and tags for populating UI filters. The security rules grant full read access without attempting to filter the results, adhering to QAP.
3.  **Tool:** The `/tools/{toolId}` collection is designed for global readability by all authenticated users (`allow list: if request.auth.uid != null`). This directly supports the 'Tool Catalog Display' feature, allowing users to browse a comprehensive catalog without rules filtering individual tools. The security rules provide the necessary broad read access, and any client-side filtering (e.g., 'show only my tools') is handled by client queries, not by the rules themselves, fully adhering to QAP.

**DBAC (Database Access Control):**
The `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection is introduced specifically for DBAC. It serves as a marker collection where the *existence* of a document at `/roles_admin/{request.auth.uid}` signifies administrative privileges. This avoids custom claims and ensures that role-based authorization is managed within the database using simple, atomic `exists()` checks in security rules.
